final_rationale: The verdict does not change. The Actor provided no new admissible evidence and mainly narrowed the claim to a caveated position based on the same record. That narrowing is analytically sound as a hypothetical: certification could become supportable with caveats if the limitation were explicitly disclosed in the final model card before launch or covered by approved risk acceptance or approved mitigation. But the present record still lacks evidence that any of those compliance predicates actually occurred. Under the policy text, clean certification requires either no remaining material weakness or an approved mitigation with owner, threshold, review date, and rollback criterion. The evidence instead shows an unresolved below-target launch-use-case slice, a draft runbook with TBD fields, and a model-card draft that still says there are no known material limitations despite reviewer concern. That means the Actor's reframing improves precision but does not convert the current record into demonstrated compliant_with_caveats. The unresolved issue is not business urgency or tone; it is the absence of admissible proof that the required disclosure or approval happened.
remaining_concerns: No admissible evidence shows the final model card was updated before launch to disclose the health-plan benefits limitation for the named launch use case.
No admissible evidence shows approved risk acceptance.
The draft runbook does not satisfy the policy elements for approved mitigation because owner and customer-notice criterion remain TBD, and no approved threshold/review record is in evidence.

The current model-card draft statement that there are no known material limitations remains in tension with the unresolved below-target benefits-support slice unless and until materiality is resolved or the limitation is explicitly disclosed.

Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents support general launch readiness, but they do not satisfy the separate disclosure or approved-mitigation predicate in the policy text.
